dedupe_keys.name: access to specialized health care services among older canadians

description: Statistics Canada describes an analysis of the Canadian Health Survey on Seniors 2019–2020 using a nationally representative sample of 39,047 people aged at least 65. The source reports use of medical specialists, non-emergency tests and surgery, together with reported difficulty accessing services. It describes latent-class analysis and gender-stratified logistic regression to analyse care needs and service use. This is a published healthcare-service information source with PDF and HTML descriptors, not a released individual-level survey dataset or executable model. The resource retains source-reported analytical methods without asserting causal effects, prediction accuracy or access to underlying microdata. The article body and numerical tables were not retrieved. The Canadian Urban Data Catalogue preserves source identifiers and descriptive metadata. Provider: Statistics Canada. Licence: Statistics Canada Open Licence Agreement. Costs and current file access are unverified. Access metadata says Open; isopen is false. No linked dataset, workbook, document, archive or model/code body was retrieved. Specific simulation applications beyond the stated role are unknown.
